//timeframes: Read per symbol, highest first. The first is treated as your bias timeframe, later ones as timing. Remove to use default_timeframe only.
//max_symbols: Safety cap on how many watchlist symbols one brief will scan (default 25).

bullish: Price is above the 20 EMA on the 4H
bearish: Price is below the 20 EMA on the 4H
neutral: Price is chopping around the 20 EMA

//strategies: Criteria as DATA, not prose. bias_criteria above are sentences a model grades by judgement — two sessions can grade them differently and they cannot be backtested. These can be checked with strategy_check, scanned across symbols with strategy_scan, and reproduced exactly. Operands: price, open, high, low, close, volume, prev_day_open/high/low/close, high_of_day, low_of_day, session_volume, pct_change_today, sma(N), ema(N), rsi(N), atr(N), and any of those followed by * / + - a number.

swing-breakout-long.description: EXAMPLE ONLY — a daily-chart swing setup transcribed from a public tutorial. It has NOT been backtested here. Run backtest_drawn or backtest_strategy before trusting it, and read the caveat below: the breakout condition it depends on is not expressible in these criteria.

criteria.note: Long-term trend filter — the setup skips anything under its 200 SMA
Short-term momentum aligned with the long-term trend
Entry is meant to be close to the 8 EMA, not extended away from it
Too far above the 8 EMA is where this setup takes profit, not where it enters

swing-breakout-long.//not_expressible: The setup's core condition — a breakout above a resistance level that was TESTED two or three times — cannot be written as a comparison, because it needs level detection rather than a value. Use levels_find for that and check its `tests` count; these criteria are the mechanical filter, not the whole setup.
swing-breakout-long.//sizing: Exits (quarters into extension, stop on a close below the 8 EMA) are trade management, not entry criteria, so they are not here.

risk_rules: Only take trades where R:R is at least 1:2
No trading in the first 15 minutes of the NY session open
If I have 2 losing trades in a row, stop for the day
notes: Add any other context you want Claude to factor in — e.g. macro events this week, key dates, anything that should affect your bias.
